label: Extreme Close-Up
clause: Fill the rectangle with a fragment of face so pores, a catchlight, and one eyebrow become the entire landscape.

label: Iris Insert
clause: Crop until a single iris, pupil, and catchlight occupy the whole pane, lashes grazing the edges.

label: Tear Insert
clause: Isolate a tear on a cheek so the droplet and skin grain replace any sense of a full face.

label: Mouth Insert
clause: Fill the pane with lips and teeth so speech becomes a moving landscape of moisture and enamel.

label: Breath Insert
clause: Crop to nostrils and upper lip so exhaled vapor or a tremor is the only action.

label: Choker
clause: Crop just under the chin and through the hairline so the neck almost vanishes and the face feels too close.

label: Ear Insert
clause: Let an ear, earring, and a strip of jaw own the rectangle, the rest of the head implied offscreen.

label: Hands Insert
clause: Fill with fingers working an object so knuckles, tendons, and the tool become the scene.

label: Handshake Insert
clause: Crop two meeting palms so the grip and ring fingers tell the deal.

label: Palm Insert
clause: Open a single palm toward the lens until creases and a held token fill the pane.

label: Fingertip Insert
clause: Magnify fingertips on a surface so prints, grit, and contact are the story.

label: Feet Insert
clause: Crop to shoes and pavement so gait, scuff, and the next step own the picture.

label: Toes Insert
clause: Isolate bare toes on tile so nails and grout lines replace the body.

label: Ankle Insert
clause: Hold ankles and hems so standing weight and a puddle tell the wait.

label: Ring Insert
clause: Magnify a ring on a finger against cloth so metal and fabric are the only readable objects.

label: Key Insert
clause: Crop a key entering a lock so bitting and the keyhole eclipse the hand.

label: Drink Insert
clause: Fill with a glass rim, liquid, and condensation so the pour is the event.

label: Document Insert
clause: Hold unmarked paper so blocks of type, a stamp, and a signature fill the pane.

label: Product Insert
clause: Pack a product so its silhouette and a specular edge sit in a clean field.

label: Label Insert
clause: Crop an unmarked bottle label so paper fiber, glue line, and letterforms are readable.

label: Screen Insert
clause: Fill with a glowing unmarked display so interface glow, not the room, owns exposure.

label: Handheld Screen
clause: Crop a handheld screen in palms so the glow lights fingers and the room falls away.

label: Clock Cutaway
clause: Cut away to a clock face so hands and numerals announce time without the people.

label: Food Insert
clause: Magnify a bite on a plate so steam, sauce, and garnish become terrain.

label: Big Close-Up
clause: Crop brow to mouth so eyes and nostrils dominate, forehead and chin clipped.

label: Close-Up
clause: Hold a face from mid-forehead to just below the chin with shoulders only hinted.

label: Medium Close-Up
clause: Cut at mid-chest so face, neck, and a collar sit with breathing room above the hair.

label: Head and Shoulders
clause: Include both shoulders and the full head so posture reads before expression.

label: Medium Shot
clause: Cut at the waist so hands can enter, belt visible, environment a muted band behind.

label: Cowboy
clause: Cut mid-thigh so a belt line, holster height, and torso read as a standing figure of action.

label: Leaner
clause: Let a figure lean into the pane from the edge so torso and face arrive while hips stay offscreen.

label: Medium Long Shot
clause: Cut at the shins so knees, stride, and most of the body read against a readable room.

label: Knee Shot
clause: Cut at the knees so gesture from thigh up is complete and the floor is only a strip.

label: Full Shot
clause: Include head to toe with a ribbon of floor and a ribbon of air so the whole costume reads.

label: Grounded Full
clause: Plant the feet on the bottom edge with almost no floor, head clearing the top by a breath.

label: Long Shot
clause: Place a full body small enough that architecture and path around them are equally important.

label: Very Long Shot
clause: Shrink the figure until clothing color becomes a speck and the street or field is the true owner.

label: Extreme Wide Shot
clause: Hold a landscape or city massing where a person is optional and weather owns the scale.

label: Extreme Long Shot
clause: Set a traveler tiny on a road or ridge so distance, not expression, is the information.

label: Interior Wide
clause: Take in ceiling, floor, and opposing walls so the room becomes a complete box around anyone inside.

label: Interior Master
clause: Cover the whole playing area of a room so every doorway, seat, and crossing is visible at once.

label: Exterior Master
clause: Hold the building, sidewalk, and approach so geography of the scene is complete before closer coverage.

label: Establishing
clause: Open on the unmarked place from outside so the audience can name the location before any face.

label: Weather Establishing
clause: Show the place under current sky so rain, haze, or glare is the first fact.

label: Aerial Establishing
clause: Survey from altitude so roof, courtyard, and surrounding streets map the site.

label: Re-establishing
clause: Return to a broader view after close coverage so the room's new blocking and emptied chairs are clear.

label: Reverse Re-establish
clause: Re-open the scene from the opposite side so previously unseen walls and exits appear.

label: Window Cutaway
clause: Cut away to a window view so outside traffic or weather comments without the speakers.

label: Crowd Cutaway
clause: Cut away to watching faces so reaction, not the action, fills the pane.

label: Sky Cutaway
clause: Cut away to unmarked sky and a roofline so time of day continues without bodies.

label: Other Hands Cutaway
clause: Cut away to someone else's hands elsewhere in the room doing a private task.

label: Prop Detail Insert
clause: Magnify a story object on a table so scratches and use-wear replace the owners.

label: Two-Shot
clause: Fit two people in one rectangle so both faces and the air between them are readable.

label: Walking Two-Shot
clause: Hold two walkers side by side so paired stride and shared path fill the width.

label: Seated Two-Shot
clause: Sit two people at a table so plates, hands, and both torsos share the pane.

label: Profile Two-Shot
clause: Face two profiles toward each other so noses and the gap between them are the axis.

label: Fifty-Fifty
clause: Split the rectangle evenly between two facing bodies so neither owns more area than the other.

label: Power Two-Shot
clause: Stand one figure over a seated other so stature, not dialogue, states the rank.

label: Stacked Two-Shot
clause: Align one head in front of another so the rear person becomes a stacked halo behind the nearer face.

label: Three-Shot
clause: Arrange three people so all faces read, typically a triangle of seats or shoulders.

label: Line Three-Shot
clause: Line three bodies across the pane so a bench or railing holds them in a row.

label: Group Shot
clause: Fit a cluster of four or more so relationships of height and huddle are visible.

label: Table Group
clause: Surround a table with a dining or meeting cluster so faces, plates, and the tabletop oval all read.

label: Crowd Wide
clause: Fill the place with a crowd so individuals melt into density and the mass is the owner.

label: Packed Crowd
clause: Compress bodies until shoulders and heads tile the rectangle with almost no ground.

label: Behind the Crowd
clause: Shoot from among backs of heads so the distant event is glimpsed through a forest of hair.

label: Isolated in Crowd
clause: Keep one sharp figure in a sea of softer bodies so isolation reads inside density.

label: Clean Single
clause: Isolate one person with empty air around them, no other body even as a blur.

label: Dirty Single
clause: Keep one person as the focus while a smear of another body or object dirties an edge.

label: Profile Single
clause: Turn one person to full profile so the nose-to-nape silhouette is the owner.

label: Profile Walker
clause: Hold a walking profile so the stride becomes a side-view cutout against the wall.

label: Dirty OTS Left
clause: Blur a foreground cheek and ear so the speaker beyond is seen past living flesh.

label: Dirty OTS Right
clause: Park a foreground jaw, collar, and shoulder mass as a dark slab the distant face must clear.

label: Clean OTS Left
clause: Aim past an empty shoulder line with no flesh in the foreground plane, the distant person clean and full.

label: Clean OTS Right
clause: Use architecture as the shoulder stand-in so the distant face is clean, no cheek in the pane.

label: Deep Over-Shoulder
clause: Keep the foreground body large and the distant person small in a doorway so depth, not equality, rules.

label: Reverse Over-Shoulder
clause: Flip to the opposite over-shoulder so the previous listener's face now owns the distant plane.

label: Front Single
clause: Face one person square to the lens so both ears are hinted and the gaze hits the glass.

label: Three-Quarter Single
clause: Turn the body forty-five degrees so one ear hides and the closer shoulder leads.

label: Open Frame
clause: Leave an exit of empty air on the travel side so the person could walk out without hitting a wall of the pane.

label: Closed Frame
clause: Box the person with door jambs, shelves, or a window grid so the world feels sealed around them.

label: Looking Room
clause: Put extra air in front of the eyes so the gaze has a place to land inside the rectangle.

label: Lead Room
clause: Put extra air in front of a moving body so the path they are about to take is visible.

label: Short-Sided
clause: Crowd the face toward the edge they stare at so the back of the head sits in empty air and the gaze feels trapped.

label: Nose Room
clause: Give a profile extra air beyond the nose so the face is not kissing the edge.

label: Foot Room
clause: Include a strip of floor beyond the toes so stance and the next step have ground.

label: Crushed Headroom
clause: Let the crown graze or break the top edge so the ceiling feels too close.

label: Generous Headroom
clause: Stack extra air above the hair so the person sits sunk and the architecture towers.

label: Doorway Frame
clause: Nest the person in a doorway so the jambs crop them as a picture inside the picture.

label: Arch Frame
clause: Nest the figure under an arch so stone or plaster curves become a second rectangle.

label: Mirror Frame
clause: Hold the person only as a reflection so the real body is offscreen and glass is the set.

label: 16:9 Presenter Headroom
clause: Sit a talking head in sixteen-by-nine with a band of empty wall above the hair and a desk line holding the lower third.

label: 16:9 Landscape
clause: Spread a place across sixteen-by-nine so the horizon sits on a third and unmarked sky becomes a lid.

label: 16:9 Conversation
clause: Fit a seated pair in sixteen-by-nine so both faces live in the middle band with lamps in the side panels.

label: 9:16 Standing Full
clause: Stack a standing person in nine-by-sixteen from shoes to hair with pavement below and sky leftover for a caption band.

label: 9:16 Face Stack
clause: Fill nine-by-sixteen with a face in the upper half and torso falling away so the chin sits above the true center.

label: 9:16 Upward Room
clause: Put a figure in the lower half of nine-by-sixteen and let building or trees rise through the tall leftover air.

label: 4:5 Face-Plate Headroom
clause: Crop a four-by-five face plate so the crown nearly kisses the top and the chest pins the bottom, shoulders almost touching sides.

label: 4:5 Three-Quarter Body
clause: Fit head-to-thighs in four-by-five so fashion length reads without empty pavement.

label: 4:5 Place Plate
clause: Stand a building in four-by-five with ground in the lower third and the facade climbing the remaining height.

label: 1:1 Centered Face
clause: Center a face in a square with equal cheek margin and the chin hovering just above the bottom edge.

label: 1:1 Product Square
clause: Center a product in a square with equal empty field so the object becomes a heraldic badge.

label: 1:1 Courtyard
clause: Map a courtyard or room in a square so floor-plan geometry, not a horizon, organizes the pane.

label: 2.39 Tiny Figure
clause: Float a small walker in a two-three-nine ribbon with empty bay or desert stretching on both sides of the body.

label: 2.39 Pair
clause: Seat two people far apart in a two-three-nine ribbon so the long silence of furniture between them is the true width.

label: 2.39 Interior Span
clause: Span a long interior in a two-three-nine ribbon so lamps recede in a line and the ceiling becomes a thin strip.

label: 1.85 Room
clause: Fit ceiling and floor of a room in one-eight-five with modest hair-to-top air so a standing person occupies the middle band.

label: 1.85 Close Face
clause: Place a close face in one-eight-five with extra side air so cheeks do not hit the edges and the background stays a thin story.

label: 1.85 Street
clause: Hold a street in one-eight-five with modest sky and readable shopfronts, less panoramic than a two-three-nine ribbon.

label: 16:9 Lower-Third Clear
clause: Keep sixteen-by-nine torso and face raised enough that the bottom fifth is empty wall or desk for later type.

label: 9:16 Lower Safe
clause: Keep nine-by-sixteen feet and hands out of the bottom fifth so interface chrome could sit on pavement.

label: 4:5 Top Safe
clause: Keep four-by-five hair below a thin top margin so the crown never clips in a four-by-five window.

label: Macro Type Insert
clause: Magnify unmarked type on packaging until letterforms are architecture.

label: Headless Torso
clause: Crop out the head so clothing, hands, and stance are the identity.

label: Over-Table Two-Shot
clause: Aim across a tabletop so glasses in the foreground field and two faces beyond the plates share focus.

label: Single Against Mass
clause: Pin one person at an edge while a crowd occupies the rest, scale stating solitude.

label: Balcony Group
clause: Arrange several people on a balcony rail so bodies stack against a drop of city.

label: Queue Line
clause: Recede a line of waiting bodies so the queue becomes a perspective machine.

label: Audience from Stage
clause: Fill with seated watchers from a stage eyeline so rows and faces are the landscape.

label: Stage from House
clause: Shoot a distant figure on a platform over a foreground of heads and seat backs.

label: Lash Insert
clause: Fill with closed lashes and lid so makeup grain and a tremor replace the eyeball.

label: Interface Insert
clause: Hold only an unmarked UI panel so buttons and a cursor, not a face, carry the beat.

label: Seated Cowboy
clause: Sit a figure so the cowboy cut still shows thighs, belt, and torso, chair arms in the sides.

label: Aerial City Extreme
clause: Map unmarked city fabric from altitude so blocks and rivers are texture and people vanish.

label: Profile Against Wall
clause: Pin a profile to a wall so the silhouette becomes a cutout and the room behind is denied.

label: High Over-Shoulder
clause: Raise the over-shoulder so we see the far scalp and notes on a table, the foreground shoulder a dark hill.

label: Low Over-Shoulder
clause: Drop the over-shoulder so the foreground back becomes a wall and the far face sits against ceiling lamps.

label: Collar Insert
clause: Crop to collar, throat, and a pulse so jewelry or a button is the landscape.

label: Watch Insert
clause: Magnify an unmarked watch face so hands, crystal, and a wrist hairline own the pane.

label: Costume Full
clause: Hold head-to-toe with generous side air so the entire costume silhouette reads as a fashion plate.

label: Glue-Line Label
clause: Magnify the glue line and paper edge of an unmarked label until packaging becomes a landscape of fiber.
